opportunities.name: Veteran Shark Tank 2026 (13th annual)
opportunities.amount: $50,000 to the winner; five veteran entrepreneurs pitch live
opportunities.summary: CLOSES 13 OCT — the best-fitting live item on the board for a company under a year old, because its age test runs the opposite way to everyone else's. Buckeye wants two years and Tadlock wants one; this one wants under three. Entry is a form plus a 2-minute narrated pitch video and a deck of no more than 10 slides covering market, product, go-to-market, customers, financials and key risks. No application fee is named anywhere on the application page. The 2016 winner was NeuroFlow, now a behavioural-health platform, so the judges have backed a health-tech company before.
opportunities.eligibility: US military veteran-owned. The business must be NO OLDER THAN THREE YEARS on the day of the competition, 7 December 2026 — an age ceiling, not a floor, which is why a company too young for most veteran grants qualifies here.
documents: Proof of veteran status (DD-214 or equivalent)
A 2-minute narrated pitch video — a pitch, not a promo
A deck of 10 slides or fewer: market, product/service, go-to-market, customers, financials, key risks
Evidence the business is under three years old as of 7 Dec 2026

opportunities.name: Army xTech|Search 10
opportunities.agency: U.S. Army FUZE xTech Program, ASA(ALT)
opportunities.amount: Up to $1,000,000 in non-dilutive cash prizes across the competition: $5,000 to each of up to 50 semifinalists, a further $20,000 to each of up to 20 finalists, then $200,000 / $100,000 / $50,000 to first, second and third. Finalists may also submit a Phase I Army SBIR or STTR proposal worth up to $300,000.
opportunities.summary: BEST LIVE ITEM ON THE BOARD, and the deadline is 19 Oct at 5pm ET. It is an OPEN-TOPIC competition — you are not fitting a product to a stated problem — and one of the four named priority portfolios is 'Immersive and Wearables: smart electronic devices that can be worn by or attached to the user to gather data or provide insight', which is Vybe's category described by the Army in its own words. Four rounds: white paper by 19 Oct, virtual semifinal pitch 18-29 Jan 2027, finals at eMerge Americas in Miami 2-4 Mar 2027, then the SBIR/STTR window to 30 Apr. THE ONE GATE TO READ CAREFULLY: technologies falling EXCLUSIVELY within the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command portfolio — military operational medicine, clinical and rehabilitative medicine, infectious disease, CBRN — are excluded. Vybe's honest position is a commercial consumer wearable with a dual-use readiness application, not a medical technology, which is both true and the only framing that clears this exclusion. Do not describe it as a medical or diagnostic capability to sound more serious; that is the sentence that makes it ineligible. Judges compare unlike technologies, so the published evaluation emphasis is commercial traction, a defensible technical advantage, a direct line to an Army need, and a credible transition path.
opportunities.eligibility: For-profit US small business, more than 50% owned AND controlled by US citizens or permanent residents, 500 or fewer employees including affiliates. The submission must not be substantially the same as a proposal funded, being funded, or pending award at another federal agency. One submission per entity. No fee, and no equity is taken.
documents: Concept white paper via the xTech portal (Section IV of the RFI PDF states the format; the PDF was not readable from here)
Eligibility attestation: for-profit, >50% US-citizen owned and controlled, <=500 employees
Disclosure of any similar proposal funded or pending at another federal agency
SAM.gov UEI and a CAGE code for the follow-on SBIR/STTR stage

opportunities.name: Ohio TechCred
opportunities.amount: up to $1,000 per employee credential, capped at $30,000 per application period
opportunities.summary: CORRECTED 30 SEP: this row previously read "Ohio-based employers only", which understates it badly. The real test is a non-residential Ohio premises plus Ohio-resident W-2 employees on the state payroll system — a three-person startup working from home, or one whose founders draw no W-2 wage, fails on both counts before the credentials are even chosen. Confirm those two facts before anything else. The window is 9:00am 1 Oct to 3:00pm 30 Oct 2026. Reimburses technology credentials for current OR prospective employees rather than funding the business, so it is a cost offset on upskilling, and the employer pays the training provider first and claims afterwards. The programme was reframed in July 2026 with a tighter technology-focused credential definition, updated employer eligibility and a new eligible-provider list, so any advice written before then is stale. The application does not ask you to name individuals — only headcounts per credential and average wages before and after. It is competitive and merit-based, not first come, first served, and reviews can take up to 90 days. Drafted as the `techcred` packet.
opportunities.eligibility: FOUR GATES, NOT ONE. The employer must be registered with the Ohio Secretary of State; must have a PHYSICAL, NON-RESIDENTIAL business location in Ohio; must employ Ohio-resident W-2 employees reported to the Ohio Unemployment Insurance Office; and must withhold Ohio income tax for them. Independent contractors and 1099 workers do not count, and an employer exempt from those reporting requirements is not eligible at all. One application per federal tax ID per period. Training must come from a provider on Ohio's eligible list, and that provider must be independent of the employer.
documents: Federal tax ID, Ohio Payee ID from ohiopays.ohio.gov, and Ohio Secretary of State charter or entity number
Physical non-residential Ohio business address and number of Ohio W-2 employees
Chosen credential from the eligible list, or a full case for a new one, with the training provider's own documentation
Per-credential training and certification costs, and the reimbursement amount requested (max $1,000 each)
Headcounts of incumbent and prospective employees per credential, with average wages before and after

opportunities.summary: THE BIGGEST OHIO AWARD ON THE BOARD AND THE ONE VYBE CANNOT APPLY FOR TODAY. The licence requirement is the whole gate: TVSF Phase 2 exists to move technology OUT of Ohio research institutions into startups, so a company that built its own stack has nothing to license and nothing to propose. That is worth a row anyway, because the gate is one Vybe could deliberately clear: the path in is a licence from an Ohio institution, and the Round 44 awards list includes the University of Akron Research Foundation, while the Kinetic programme already on this board is a partnership with NEOMED. A licence taken for its own sake would be a bad idea; a licence Vybe actually wants would unlock a $200K grant round every quarter. Rounds run quarterly: Round 46's RFP was released 24 July 2026, proposals were due 4pm on 6 August, awards around October 2026, which puts the next RFP around late October and a deadline in early November — check the page rather than the pattern. The proposal is seven pages, plus a required one-page letter of support, and no appendices are allowed. Personnel costs cannot exceed 20% of the budget, and travel, legal, licensing and royalty fees are ineligible expenses.
opportunities.eligibility: BLOCKED FOR VYBE AS IT STANDS. An Ohio-based for-profit with a physical Ohio principal place of business under a lease of 12 months or more — AND the project's technology must be one the company has licensed, or intends to license, FROM an Eligible Institution: an Ohio university, an Ohio not-for-profit research institution, or a federal lab. The technology must already carry IP protection (patent pending or issued; for IT, trade secret, trademark or copyright). A signed exclusive licence must be produced within nine months of applying.
